title: Sunny and the First Star | Bedtime Story
description: Little Sunny the quokka stands very still at dusk and waits patiently for the very first star of the night to appear. A peaceful, wonder-filled bedtime story from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
The sky was turning from orange to pink to a soft pale blue.

Little Sunny the quokka sat very still at the top of a gentle grassy hill and watched.

She was waiting for something.

Every evening, there was one single star that appeared before all the others. Just one — blinking awake in the early dark like a tiny eye opening for the first time.

Sunny wanted to see the exact moment it appeared.

She sat. She waited. She did not fidget.

The sky grew deeper. The last orange faded from the edges of the clouds.

And then — there.

A tiny point of light. So small. So steady. The very first star of the night.

Sunny let out a long slow breath.

"There you are," she whispered.

She made her wish then — the same wish she always made. Not for something big. Just for a good sleep. And nice dreams. And to wake up to another gentle morning.

She watched the first star a little longer.

Then the second star appeared. And the third. And slowly, slowly, more came — until the whole sky above her was sprinkled with soft, quiet light.

Sunny lay back in the cool grass and looked up at all of them.

So many stars. So much sky. All of it still and kind.

Her eyes grew heavy, the way they always did when she lay still and looked at something very beautiful for a long time.

One by one, she stopped counting the stars.

One by one, the stars kept watch.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, first star. Goodnight, little one.
